sections.title: Foundations (Stages 1–2)
sections.description: The first computing ideas that everything else is built on.

questions.question: What is an algorithm?
questions.options: A kind of computer screen | A set of steps, in order, that solves a problem or gets a task done | A photograph of a computer | A game you can only play online
questions.correctAnswer: A set of steps, in order, that solves a problem or gets a task done
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a list of clear steps in the right order — a computer follows them one by one to do a job.

questions.question: In Scratch, what usually happens when you click the green flag?
questions.options: The sprite is deleted for ever | The computer turns itself off | The program starts running from the beginning | The project is printed on paper
questions.correctAnswer: The program starts running from the beginning
questions.explanation: The green flag is the start signal. Blocks joined under ‘when green flag clicked’ begin to run from the top.

questions.question: Which of these is hardware?
questions.options: a maths game program | a drawing app | a keyboard | a website
questions.correctAnswer: a keyboard
questions.explanation: Hardware is the part of a computer you can touch, like a keyboard. Apps, programs and websites are software.

questions.question: A speaker is which kind of device?
questions.options: An input device — it puts your voice into the computer | A cooling device — it keeps the computer cold | A storage device — it keeps your files | An output device — it sends sound out of the computer
questions.correctAnswer: An output device — it sends sound out of the computer
questions.explanation: Output devices send information out to us. A speaker sends sound out, so it is an output device.

questions.question: A bar chart shows the fruit a class likes best: mango 8 votes, banana 5 votes, apple 3 votes. Which fruit has the tallest bar?
questions.options: mango | apple | they are all the same height | banana
questions.correctAnswer: mango
questions.explanation: The tallest bar belongs to the biggest number. Mango has 8 votes, and 8 is the biggest, so its bar is tallest.

questions.question: A class wants to collect the outdoor temperature every day for a week. Which device would help most?
questions.options: a digital thermometer that measures temperature | a skipping rope | a pair of sunglasses | a paintbrush
questions.correctAnswer: a digital thermometer that measures temperature
questions.explanation: Computing devices with sensors, like a digital thermometer, can measure and record data for us every day.

questions.question: Two algorithms both draw the same square. One uses 4 steps and the other uses 12 steps. Which algorithm is more efficient?
questions.options: The 4-step one, because it does the same job with fewer steps | They are equally efficient | The 12-step one, because more steps are always better | Neither one can draw a square
questions.correctAnswer: The 4-step one, because it does the same job with fewer steps
questions.explanation: Efficient means doing the same job with fewer steps. Both draw the square, so the 4-step algorithm is more efficient.

questions.question: What is a network?
questions.options: A drawing of a spider’s web on paper | One computer with nothing connected to it | Computers and devices connected together so they can share things | A special kind of keyboard
questions.correctAnswer: Computers and devices connected together so they can share things
questions.explanation: A network is a group of computers and devices joined together so they can share messages, pictures and files.

questions.question: Someone you do not know sends you a message online asking for your home address. What should you do?
questions.options: Do not share it, and tell a trusted grown-up about the message | Share it, because it is polite to answer | Share it only if they ask twice | Post your address where everyone can see it
questions.correctAnswer: Do not share it, and tell a trusted grown-up about the message
questions.explanation: Your name and address are private. Never share them with strangers online — and always tell a trusted grown-up.

questions.question: Amina’s Scratch story starts in a bedroom scene and then moves to a park. What should her program change to show the park?
questions.options: the volume of the speakers | the computer’s battery | the backdrop | the colour of the mouse
questions.correctAnswer: the backdrop
questions.explanation: The backdrop is the big picture behind the sprites. Switching the backdrop changes the scene of the story.

questions.question: What is a file on a computer?
questions.options: A row of children lining up | A saved piece of work, like a story or a picture, kept with its own name | A metal tool for smoothing wood | A button that turns the screen on
questions.correctAnswer: A saved piece of work, like a story or a picture, kept with its own name
questions.explanation: When you save your work, the computer keeps it as a file with a name, so you can find and open it again later.

questions.question: Which of these is an Internet of Things device?
questions.options: A paper notebook | A football | A smart fridge that sends a message when the milk runs out | A wooden spoon
questions.correctAnswer: A smart fridge that sends a message when the milk runs out
questions.explanation: Internet of Things devices are everyday things with tiny computers that connect to the internet — like a smart fridge.

questions.question: Khalid changes one step near the start of his music program. What can happen to the rest of the program?
questions.options: Nothing can ever change | Only the screen’s brightness changes | The program deletes itself | The whole program can behave differently, because later steps depend on earlier ones
questions.correctAnswer: The whole program can behave differently, because later steps depend on earlier ones
questions.explanation: Steps in a program run in order, so changing one early step can change everything that comes after it.

questions.question: In a secret code (a cipher), what is the ciphertext?
questions.options: The computer’s screen | The scrambled, secret version of the message | The person who sends the message | A kind of printer
questions.correctAnswer: The scrambled, secret version of the message
questions.explanation: A cipher turns your normal message (plain text) into a scrambled secret version — that scrambled version is the ciphertext.

questions.question: Why do game developers break a big project into smaller sub-tasks?
questions.options: Small tasks are easier to plan, build and test one at a time | It uses up more electricity | It makes the game impossible to finish | It makes the computer heavier
questions.correctAnswer: Small tasks are easier to plan, build and test one at a time
questions.explanation: Breaking a big task into sub-tasks makes each part easier to think about — you can build and test one piece at a time.

questions.question: Sara’s chase game has a bug: her sprite moves left when she presses the right arrow key. What should she do first?
questions.options: Delete the whole game and start again | Buy a new computer | Press the key harder | Look carefully at the blocks for the right arrow and fix the wrong one
questions.correctAnswer: Look carefully at the blocks for the right arrow and fix the wrong one
questions.explanation: Debugging means finding the exact block that is wrong and fixing it — you do not need to throw the game away.

questions.question: In a spreadsheet, what is a cell?
questions.options: One box where a row and a column meet | The computer’s battery | The on/off button | A telephone call
questions.correctAnswer: One box where a row and a column meet
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet is made of rows and columns. Each little box where a row and a column meet is called a cell.

questions.question: Fatima tests her program and it does not do what she planned. What is the best next step?
questions.options: Hide the program so nobody sees it | Decide the computer is broken | Never test a program again | Find the bug, fix it, then test the program again
questions.correctAnswer: Find the bug, fix it, then test the program again
questions.explanation: Testing is how we find bugs. When a test shows a problem, we fix the bug and test again until it works.

questions.question: In ScratchJr, how do you build a program?
questions.options: Draw the program on paper only | Join blocks together in the right order | Type long sentences of code | Shake the tablet until it works
questions.correctAnswer: Join blocks together in the right order
questions.explanation: In ScratchJr you snap picture blocks together in a row — the character follows the blocks in order.

questions.question: Rahma sorts her toy animals into two groups: farm animals and wild animals. What is she doing with her data?
questions.options: Emailing it | Sorting it into groups | Deleting it | Printing it
questions.correctAnswer: Sorting it into groups
questions.explanation: Putting things into groups that belong together is called sorting — it makes data much easier to understand.

questions.question: Which of these is a computer?
questions.options: a sandwich | a tablet | a stone | a wooden chair
questions.correctAnswer: a tablet
questions.explanation: A tablet is a computer — it has a screen, runs programs and follows instructions. The others are not computers.

questions.question: Which device usually joins a network without any wires?
questions.options: A paper book | A crayon | A wooden ruler | A smartphone using Wi-Fi
questions.correctAnswer: A smartphone using Wi-Fi
questions.explanation: Wireless devices like smartphones use Wi-Fi to join a network through the air — no cable needed.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Devices That Talk to Each Other

questions.question: Which of these is numerical data (data made of numbers)?
questions.options: The smell of flowers | A feeling of happiness | The sound of rain | The ages of the children in a class
questions.correctAnswer: The ages of the children in a class
questions.explanation: Numerical data is made of numbers you can count or add up — like ages: 6, 7, 7, 8.

questions.question: Which of these is private information you should keep safe online?
questions.options: your favourite colour | your home address | your favourite fruit | the name of a storybook
questions.correctAnswer: your home address
questions.explanation: Your home address tells strangers where you live, so it is private. Favourite colours and fruits are safe to share.

questions.question: A robot follows its program and bumps into a wall. What caused the mistake?
questions.options: The robot’s own thinking | The weather | The instructions in its program | Bad luck
questions.correctAnswer: The instructions in its program
questions.explanation: Computers and robots do not think for themselves — they only follow instructions. If it bumps the wall, the program’s steps need fixing.

questions.question: Which of these is a computer you can carry in your pocket?
questions.options: a desk | a window | a shoe | a smartphone
questions.correctAnswer: a smartphone
questions.explanation: A smartphone is a small computer — it runs apps and follows instructions, and it fits in your pocket.

questions.question: A block graph shows the class’s favourite pets, and the row for cats is the longest. What does that tell you?
questions.options: Cats got the fewest votes | Nobody chose cats | The graph is broken | Cats got the most votes
questions.correctAnswer: Cats got the most votes
questions.explanation: In a block graph, the longest row shows the biggest count — so cats got the most votes.

questions.question: What is the internet?
questions.options: A kind of food | A place you can walk to | The biggest network of all, joining computers around the world | One single tablet
questions.correctAnswer: The biggest network of all, joining computers around the world
questions.explanation: The internet is a giant network that connects computers all around the world so they can share things.

questions.question: To wash your hands you: wet your hands, rub with soap, rinse, then dry. What kind of list is this?
questions.options: A picture | A song | A shopping list | Steps in order, like an algorithm
questions.correctAnswer: Steps in order, like an algorithm
questions.explanation: It is a list of steps in the right order — just like an algorithm. Doing the steps out of order would not work well.

questions.question: Yusuf’s dance algorithm has the moves in the wrong order, so the dance looks wrong. What should he do?
questions.options: Add more wrong steps | Put the steps back in the right order | Turn the music louder | Give up dancing
questions.correctAnswer: Put the steps back in the right order
questions.explanation: Order matters in an algorithm. Putting the steps back in the right order will fix the dance.
